### Context

A timing trace showed two four-minute scans that returned identical file lists.

### What is broken

The automatic check job spends its last four minutes redoing work. It scans the code for rule violations, then scans the same files again to build the final summary.

### Why it is broken

The step that builds the summary starts its own scan instead of reusing the first scan's results. In a trial, giving the summary the first scan's results removed the extra four minutes, and the summary stayed the same.

### How to fix it

Pass the first scan's list of results to the summary instead of scanning again. The job then finishes four minutes sooner with the same output. Choose hotfix because this changes the one place in the code that starts the second scan.

gauntlet: gate=chase-bug/verdict-menu recommended=2

### Context

Inspecting the heading in the browser showed that a different font was drawing the letter "z".

### What is broken

A slide heading that contains the letter "z" spills out of its card.

### Why it is broken

The heading font has no drawing for "z", so the browser borrows a wider font for that letter. This widens the heading from 280 to 312 pixels, but the card is only 300 pixels wide. In a trial with a complete font, the heading stayed at 280 pixels, inside its card.

### How to fix it

Replace the heading font file with a complete version that includes "z", and leave the card width unchanged. The change is small, but the font file is kept outside this repository. Its owner must supply the new version, and this repository's tests cannot check it. Choose brainstorm because the swap needs coordination with the font's owner.

Pick one:

```text
1. [ ] File a ticket - /skill:shape-ticket, seeded with this evidence.
2. [x] Brainstorm now - /skill:brainstorming with this evidence as the seed. [recommended]
3. [ ] Implement hotfix now - follow hotfix.md; add "as a PR" for a PR.
4. [ ] Finish with rendered summary.

not eligible: predicate 6 - the existing tests cannot check the changed external font file
```

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and repairs the one Before missed: Before leaned on unexplained shorthand ("CI job", "lint step") while After says "automatic check job" and "scans the code for rule violations", so a reader needs no outside knowledge. The sectioned shape stayed well under 180 words, each section is a single paragraph, Context carries only a one-line observation with no status or search result, and both gates still end at the eligibility line with the menus unchanged. One thing to watch in the After wording: it dropped the file identifiers entirely, yet the contract says to trail a citation when the reader's next action requires opening it; for Checkpoint 1 the recommended pick is a hotfix at one call site, so ending the How to fix it sentence with "(the summary builder, tools/check-job.mjs:73)" would serve that next action without reintroducing jargon. Also consider making Context carry the surviving explanation alongside the repro line (e.g. "...identical file lists; reusing the first list removed the delay") so the section earns its place as more than a restatement of What is broken.

Everything Before kept, After keeps: both checkpoints use the three fixed headings with one paragraph per section, stay well under 180 words, explain the repeated scan, four wasted minutes and result reuse, and the missing character drawing, wider substitute, 312-versus-300 overflow and font replacement in everyday words, name components by role, omit Context (accepted) and carry no citations, which is fine since the reader's next action does not require opening a file. Menus are intact in both, with hotfix alone recommended at row 2 in Checkpoint 1 and Brainstorm now alone at row 2 in Checkpoint 2 with Finish with rendered summary last and the not-eligible line naming predicate 6. Two small polish points for the After wording that do not move any fact: the Checkpoint 1 eligibility line dropped the count ('all six predicates pass' is more verifiable than 'all predicates pass'), and the Checkpoint 2 not-eligible line could keep 'the other five predicates pass' so the reader knows exactly how many were judged, matching the Preserve-menu-recommendation clause of the Change.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and additionally satisfies plain-reader: the second Before report compressed the fix to "swaps in a complete font" and never said the card width stays as it is, so a reader could not tell from the text that the remedy was the font rather than the card; After's How-to-fix section states "leave the card width alone" explicitly, names the summary step and heading font by role, keeps citations trailing in parentheses, and stays unfenced with no arrow chains. Both After reports land around 115-125 words from first heading to Pick one:, each section is a single paragraph, Context is two lines of repro and blocked-check status, menus are byte-identical in structure to Before (three rows / four rows, correct recommended row, correct last row, eligibility lines naming predicate 6), and nothing follows the eligibility fence. The one soft spot worth a wording nudge in the contract: After's closing because-clause leans on "every predicate passes" and "predicate 6" without ever saying in everyday words what a predicate is; a line such as "one of the six hotfix checks fails: this repository's tests cannot verify the external font" would keep the plain-reader fact robust across cases where the eligibility line is the only place the term appears.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: both gates use the fixed What is broken / Why it is broken / How to fix it headings, each section is a single paragraph, the mechanisms are named by role with citations trailing, and each third section closes with the recommended pick plus one because-clause while the menus and eligibility lines are untouched.
